questions.question: A can do three-fourth of a work in 12 days and B can do four-fifth of the same work in 20 days. In how many days can they complete the whole work, working together?
questions.solution:
Given:

A can do three-fourth of a work in 12 days and B can do four-fifth of the same work in 20 days.

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day × Total time taken 

Calculation:

In the case of A,

3/4 of the work A does in = 12 days

So, the total work A does in = 12 ÷ 3/4 = 16 days

In the case of B,

4/5 of the work B does in = 20 days

So, the total work B does in = 20 ÷ 4/5 = 25 days

LCM (16, 25) = 400

Let the total work be the LCM of the time taken by different workers.

So, total work = 400 units

The efficiency of A = 400/16 = 25 units a day

The efficiency of B = 400/25 = 16 units a day

Now, the time taken by them to complete the work together

⇒ 400/(25 + 16)

⇒ 9(31)/(41) days

**∴ In 9(31)/(41) days they can complete the whole work, working together.**

questions.question: A, B and C individually can complete a work in 12, 10 and 15 days, respectively. All three work together and after 3 days, B and C leave the work. The remaining work will be completed by A in:
questions.solution:
Given:

A, B and C individually can complete a work in 12, 10 and 15 days respectively

All three work together and after 3 days, B and C leave the work.

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency × Total Time

Calculation:

LCM (12, 10, 15) = 60

Let the total work be 60 units (∵ LCM of 12, 10, 15 = 60)

Efficiency of A = 60/12 = 5 units/day

Efficiency of B = 60/10 = 6 units/day

Efficiency of C = 60/15 = 4 units/day

Work done in 3 days by A, B, C = 3 × (5 + 6 + 4) = 45 units

Time required by A to complete the remaining work

⇒ (60 - 45)/5 = 3 days

**∴ The remaining work will be completed by A in 3 days.**

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 24 days. B and C together can complete it in 30 days. If the efficiency of A is twice that of C, then in how many days will B alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B together can do a piece of work in 24 days. B and C together can complete it in 30 days

The efficiency of A is twice that of C.

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day × Total time taken

Calculation:

LCM (24, 30) = 120 units

Let efficiencies of A, B, and C be represented by A, B, and C respectively.

So, A = 2C

According to the question,

A + B = 120/24

⇒ A + B = 5

⇒ 2C + B = 5 ....(1)

B + C = 120/30

⇒ B + C = 4 ....(2)

(1) - (2),

2C + B - B - C = 5 - 4

⇒ C = 1

Putting C = 1 in (2),

B = 3

Now, B will alone complete the work in = 120/3

⇒ 40 days

∴ B alone will complete the work in 40 days.

questions.question: 'A' alone can do a piece of work in 10 days and 'B' alone can do it in 15 days. 'A' and 'B' undertook to do the work for ₹42,000. With the help of 'C', they completed the work in 5 days. How much (in ₹) is to be paid to C?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A alone can do the work in 10 days.

B alone can do the work in 15 days.

**Concept used:**

Total work = LCM of time taken by each person

**Calculation:**

LCM of 10 and 15 = 30 i.e total work

Efficiency of A = 30/10 = 3

Efficiency of B = 30/15 = 2

With the assistance of C they finished the work in 5 days.

Efficiency of A, B and C is 30/5 = 6

⇒ A + B + C = 6

⇒ C = 6 – 2 – 3 = 1

Their efficiency ratio is A : B : C = 3 : 2 : 1

Share of C = (1/6) × 42000 = 7000

**∴ Share of C is Rs. 7000**

questions.question: 5 men and 6 women can earn ₹10,500 in 6 days. 8 men and 12 women can earn ₹24,800 in 8 days. In how many days will 7 men and 10 women earn ₹26,500?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

5 men and 6 women can earn ₹10,500 in 6 days. 

8 men and 12 women can earn ₹24,800 in 8 days. 

**Calculation:**

5 men and 6 women can earn Rs. 10500 in 6 days

5 men and 6 women can earn Rs. 1750 in 1 day

10 men and 12 women can earn Rs. 3500 in 1 day

Again,

8 men and 12 women can earn Rs. 24800 in 8 days

8 men and 12 women can earn Rs. 3100 in 1 day

So, 2 men can earn in 1 day = (3500 - 3100) = 400

1 man can earn Rs. 200 in 1 day

1 woman can earn in 1 day = (1750 - 1000)/6 = 125

So,

7 men and 10 women earn in 1 day = 200 × 7 + 10 × 125

⇒ 1400 + 1250

⇒ 2650

So, they will earn 26500 in 26500/2650 = 10 days

**∴ Required time is 10 days**

questions.question: A can do 40% of a work in 24 days, and B can do **33(1)/(3)**% of the same work in 15 days. They work together for 15 days, C alone completes the remaining work in 10 days. A and C together can complete 35% of the same work in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do 40% of a work in 24 days

B can do 33(1)/(3)% of the same work in 15 days

**Concept used:**

Work done = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f59931ae21f7da286dc902968332ae89703c8c804e5591736eba1d1a86b8d2fb.png] **

A can do 100% work = (24/40) × 100 = 60 days

B can do 100% work = (15/33(1)/(3)) × 100 = 45 days

Total work = 180 (LCM of 60 and 45)

Total work done by A and B in 1 day = 3 + 4 = 7 units

A and B complete works in 15 days = 7 × 15 = 105 units

Remaining work = 180 - 105 = 75 units

C can do work in 1 day = 75/10 = 7.5 units

35% of total work = 180 × (35/100) = 63 units

Time taken by A and C to complete 63 unit work = 63/(3 + 7.5) = 63/10.5 = 6 days

**∴ A and C together can complete 35% of the same work in 6 days**

questions.question: A is 30% more efficient than B. If B finishes a work in 13 days, then in how many days will A finish the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A is 30% more efficient than B

Time taken by B to finish the work = 13 days

**Concept used:**

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time when the work done is constant.

**Calculation:**

Ratio of efficiency of A and B = 130 : 100

⇒ 13 : 10

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time when the work done is constant.

⇒ Ratio of time taken by A and B = 10 : 13

Let A takes x days to do the same job

⇒ 10 : 13 : : x : 13

⇒ 10/13 : : x/13

⇒ x = (10/13 × 13)

⇒ x = 10 days

**∴ The time taken by A to finish the job is 10 days**
